title: Concept 50: production plan (10 camps x 5 ads, aiming at ROAS 5)

money.now: catalogue carousels are the account's engine; F2 4.74x (PLAYBOOK); recent good campaigns about 2.2
money.target: ROAS 5 = catalogue-level cost per purchase (₹350-490) on a basket with 40-50% three-piece orders
examples: 40% 3-piece / 20% 2-piece / 40% single → order value about ₹1,760 → ROAS 5 at about ₹350 a purchase

camps.name: FOR ~~DIDI~~ ME. (the gift list, corrected)
camps.sources: typewit-3 (rank 1 of 24). Kept: the struck relationship word, product-only frames, 'two to gift, one to keep', the reversed men's set. Changed: opens on DIDI, never THE BRIDE (all three experts); Serpentine Silver replaces the Verdant Eternity to spread the allocation; the Prism card becomes BETI (the daughter who borrows everything) so four different people on her list are named; struck words kept to 4-6 letters so they read at 200 px. Graft: 'and one for me' from roas5-5.
camps.insight: In wedding season and December she is the family's gift buyer and the one person missing from her own list. Every woman 35-44 knows the moment the gift fits her better. One struck word turns that guilty pleasure into a confession she forwards to her sister, and puts the BUY3 maths in human terms: two to gift, one to keep (Harvey Nichols' 'Sorry, I spent it on myself', localised).
camps.pictureDevice: Monument macro (A4): one piece, magnified, centred, on its own proven dark token ground, true contact shadow, one hard specular. These are the b03-1 / b03-2 / b02-5 frames that won the clean blind 200 px read. No gift box or packaging is generated.
camps.typeDevice: Velista 'FOR' + a relationship word struck by one confident hand-drawn 8 px inline-SVG line at a slight upward angle, in the piece's accent (gold-light #E4C889 or the sampled stone colour) + 'ME.' in that same accent. The strike only ever falls on a word, never a numeral or a price (so it can never read as a compare-at price). Card 5 moves the strike onto the quantity: BUY ~~ONE~~ THREE.
camps.brandDevice: 'ME.' is always the accent word; wordmark top-centre; F2 card at the foot. Primary text opens 'Bought for them. Kept by me.' and ends 'Two to gift, one to keep: 20% off any three with BUY3.'
camps.palette: plum (Cushion) · charcoal (Serpentine Silver) · terracotta (Brushed) · ink (Prism) · oxblood (Woven)
camps.buyers: Women 35-44 first (the family gift buyer), then 45-54 and 25-34 (Secret Santa). Men 18-24 through the reversed ad set (same pictures, FOR ~~ME~~ HER / MAA / DIDI).
camps.roas: Gift season is when she spends, but on others; this gives her permission to add herself, so the basket is gifts plus one = BUY3 by definition. Woven + Brushed + Cushion ₹2,747 → ₹2,198 after BUY3: ROAS 5 at a cost per purchase up to ₹440. Prism + Woven + Cushion ₹4,447 → ₹3,558: up to ₹712. Serpentine Silver + Brushed + Woven ₹2,647 → ₹2,118: up to ₹424. Every frame is the proven product-only kind, so the cost side should sit at catalogue level.
camps.carousel: Cards 1-5 as below (ring, neck, ear, wrist, ear), one series of grounds, each card linked to its product page; card 5 (BUY ~~ONE~~ THREE) links to a BUY3 collection.
risks: A struck word next to a number reads as compare-at: keep the strike 200+ px away from the price and the offer box.
Relationship jokes can sting: no saas, no husband, no religious relative; the tone stays warm ('it suited me first').
Serpentine Silver: an added jump ring between bail and basket (b04-4h) - verify at 2x zoom.
BETI could read as taking from her daughter: the beat makes it the daughter's habit ('she'll borrow it anyway'); the panel checks it; fallback DIDI.
Woven: scale and the invented bottom loop.
camps.loopWatch: Does the strike read at 200 px? Does the customer panel name three pieces for the basket? Does any persona read it as taking from someone?

camps.name: LAST PRICE? (the haggle, answered by the piece)
camps.sources: roas5-2 (rank 2) with typewit-6 SET IN merged into it (both put the price in the piece; the experts said run only one). Graft: typewit-4's '[Mummy, off screen: teeno le lo.]' as the Story alternate on card 5. Changed: 'ROUND FIGURE? already is.' was untrue over ₹999 and is rewritten; every reply is a craft truth, and only card 5 mentions a saving; luxury craft (cocoa, Cormorant numerals, restraint) answers Meera's 'bargain stall' worry; English twins for the south.
camps.insight: She bargains by reflex ('last price?', 'round figure kar do'). Online she can't, so a fixed ₹1,049 feels like an opening bid and she leaves to think. Give her the haggle and let the piece answer it: the live price sits inside the piece's own opening (VW 'Think Small' with the empty space inside the product), and the only concession is the code for three. BUY3 becomes the bargain she won.
camps.pictureDevice: The piece's empty opening, shot square-on, as the frame for its price (in-piece type). Hoops and the huggie face the lens; the toggle ring and the Prism circle lie flat under a top-down camera; the ring is seen from about 25-30° above its equator so its band reads as a slightly flattened oval that holds the price. The opening is generated empty and clean: no fingers, threads, props or reflections inside it. Every frame keeps the piece's full extent at or under 540 px tall (the RULINGS 550 px gate for a headline plus a card), which caps a round piece seen face-on at about half the Feed width, so each price is sized to its opening at that scale. The cocoa is deep and matte, as dark as espresso (b03: a mid-tone cocoa read drab), so the gold tone separates from it.
camps.typeDevice: One haggle across the swipe in Velista (LAST PRICE? › ROUND FIGURE? › THODA KAM? › PAKKA? › TEEN LO. BEES PERCENT KAM.). The shop's answer is the live price in Cormorant Garamond 500 inside the opening, sized to fit it with at least 30 px clear of metal (about 80-100 px; each card gives its size); for earrings 'the pair' goes in the beat, not the opening; a Cormorant italic reply, set directly under the Velista line in the top band (never under the piece, where the 540 px extent and the card leave no room), states a listing truth.
camps.brandDevice: 'The price ring': the live price set inside the piece in Naira's serif becomes a Naira-only signature. One cocoa ground (F2's) on all five; F2 card without a repeated price.
camps.buyers: Women 35-44 and 45-54 (price-checks first, haggles on instinct); women 25-34 for the wit; men 18-24 see a clear gift price under ₹1,000.
camps.roas: The price is the first read, so clicks qualify themselves and fewer leave over 'how much?'. The sentence pulls her through five cards to the offer, which is catalogue behaviour. Woven + Toggle + Halo Curve ₹2,947 → ₹2,358: ROAS 5 at up to ₹472 a purchase. Brushed + Woven + Toggle ₹2,747 → ₹2,198: up to ₹440. Prism + Woven + Toggle ₹4,447 → ₹3,558: up to ₹712.
camps.carousel: Cards in sentence order; each card links to its product page; card 5 links to a BUY3 collection. The sentence makes the swipe.
risks: Bazaar humour can read down-market (Meera): no red, no bursts, no 'only', no sums; the replies are dignified.
The opening must render empty and round enough for the price: say 'the opening is empty, plain cocoa shows through it'. Verify the clear margin in px.
Toggle open clasp: ring stays a sailor ring, bar 0.6-0.7x and lying beside it, not crossing the opening.
Hinglish lines may land weaker in the south: run the English twin ad set.
Price staleness: live prices at build; never a compare-at, a strike on a price, or a total.
camps.loopWatch: Does any persona read it as cheap or as a sale? Is the price legible at 200 px? Does 'TEEN LO' get read as the offer?

camps.name: YOUR LEFT HAND IS INVITED. (one piece per function)
camps.sources: rituals-3 (rank 3) copy voice, merged with roas5-1 DRESS CODE (rank 6) picture device, as the performance expert advised. Graft: typewit-2 ITINERARY's 'three functions, three looks' in the primary text. Changed: the formal 'requests the pleasure' line moves to the Story only (too much text at 200 px); the Feed carries one H1 plus a dress-code beat; every piece is paired with a function colour it contrasts with (no gold on marigold, no silver on rani pink; red-team note: the gold-tone Monochrome sits on turmeric darkened to ochre, darker than the gold tone, so its C separates while the black and white stripes carry the contrast); a neutrality lock in every prompt; card 1 is the mehendi ring, the best line in the set.
camps.insight: From now to February she gets a wedding card a week, and every card is five functions, five outfits and one question: what goes on my ears and hands at each? The jewellery sends the invitation, in the formal wording every Indian card uses, to one body part for one function. One piece per function is rotation, not a stack, and three functions make BUY3 a plan instead of a discount.
camps.pictureDevice: Tone-on-tone colour flood: the ground and one function object are dyed the function's colour, so the piece is the only thing in the frame that is not that colour (selective colour by art direction, honest and readable at 200 px). One object per card: a mehendi cone, dry turmeric, fuchsia gota silk, bridal-red silk with a thin zari edge, midnight velvet.
camps.typeDevice: Jost caps tag 'MEHENDI · 1 OF 5' top-left; Velista H1 in the invitation voice; Cormorant italic beat 'to the mehendi. dress code: green.'; Story only adds the formal line 'The Cushion Halo Ring requests the pleasure of your left hand.' inside a gold-light double hairline.
camps.brandDevice: Naira hosts the season: wordmark top-centre like a family crest, the same tag position and hairline on every card, F2 card at the foot. Primary text 'Five functions. Three looks. One order.'
camps.palette: mehendi green · turmeric yellow · rani pink · bridal red · midnight blue
camps.buyers: Women 35-44 (three weddings, five functions each), 45-54 (mother of the bride or groom), 25-34 (the bride's friends). Men 18-24 only via card 1 as an engagement gift.
camps.roas: The functions have dates, so she buys for an event. One large priced piece per card is catalogue behaviour (most of the account's purchases). Cushion + Circlet + Prism ₹4,297 → ₹3,438 after BUY3: ROAS 5 at up to ₹688 a purchase. Cushion + Monochrome + Bold Nocturne ₹3,297 → ₹2,638: up to ₹528. Scale rule: scale if 30%+ of its orders are 3+ pieces.
camps.carousel: Function order with the strongest card first: Mehendi, Haldi, Sangeet, Shaadi, Reception. Card 5 (Reception, RSVP: any three) links to a BUY3 collection.
risks: Colour casts from the floods: green on the Cushion's metal, yellow on the white enamel, pink on clear pavé, red on the white shell pearls. Every prompt carries the neutrality lock; verify at zoom.
Props must stay lighter than the piece: tone on tone, never a second bright shape.
Generic occasion lines have lost: every H1 names a body part or a truth; the occasion stays the second beat.
No religious marks, no Ganesh, no puja objects; function names are cultural only.
Bold Nocturne at the stock floor (20).
camps.loopWatch: Does the Feed read without the formal line? Do the floods cast? Does the panel plan three functions = three pieces?

camps.name: KAHAN SE LIYA? (the piece is the punctuation)
camps.sources: typewit-1 (rank 8). Changed: one series ground (deep peacock teal) instead of five; the '&' card is now the men's lead card and is proved by meaning (toi-et-moi = you and me) as much as by shape; the BUY3 anchor named in the primary text is the Toggle (77), not the Pearl (25); an English twin for the south ('WHERE IS / IT FROM'); one redo budgeted for the bracket rotation.
camps.insight: How people talk about her jewellery comes in punctuation: the aunty's 'Kahan se liya?', the 'Arre wah!', the aside '(goes with everything)', and the full stop that ends the debate. In each ad one piece is that mark, drawn three to four times taller than the words. The joke flatters her (people will ask) and the piece is the biggest, brightest shape at 200 px. The 'Where is this from?' reel hook had a high click-through rate with a creator as the hero; here the product is the hero.
camps.pictureDevice: The piece laid as a giant punctuation glyph: the Toggle chain as a question mark (the ring as the dot), the Monochrome pair as round brackets, the Halo Curve standing between two words as the ampersand, the Serpentine laid flat as an exclamation mark (the stone as the dot), one Pearl stud as the full stop. Honest magnification with a size line. Every glyph keeps its full extent at or under 540 px tall inside the picture band, and a chain leaves the frame only through the left or right edge inside that band (red-team change: the earlier '?' at 70% of the frame height and the '!' hanging from the top edge ran through the headline and card zones and failed the RULINGS gate).
camps.typeDevice: 1-3 Velista words at cap 110-120 beside the piece-glyph, at least 30 px clear; the type never draws the hero mark, the piece always does. Cards 1 and 4 set their words above the glyph (P1), because their chains leave through a side edge; cards 2, 3 and 5 set them beside it (P2). Cormorant italic second beat with a listing truth. Roman-letter Hinglish only.
camps.brandDevice: Naira owns the oversized mark: across the series a Naira piece is always the punctuation and the type never is. One deep teal ground; F2 card; primary text signed 'Naira, punctuated.'
camps.palette: one series ground: deep peacock teal #1F4A4C
camps.buyers: Women 35-44 (she is the one asked 'kahan se liya?'), women 25-34 (type wit, saves the post); men 18-24 through the TU & MAIN card in their own ad set.
camps.roas: Each mark answers one hesitation: ? = social approval, ( ) = versatility, & = a gift, ! = a statement at ₹899, . = the offer. Toggle + Monochrome + Pearl ₹3,197 → ₹2,558 after BUY3: ROAS 5 at up to ₹512 a purchase. Toggle + Halo Curve + Serpentine Silver ₹2,797 → ₹2,238: up to ₹448.
camps.carousel: ? › ( ) › & › ! › . (the sentence ends on the offer). 4:5 carousel; card 5 links to a BUY3 collection.
risks: The '?' chain: open paperclip links at about 8-10 px/mm and the exact toggle ring; drawn smaller, the 4 mm chain is lost at 200 px, drawn larger, the glyph passes the 540 px cap.
The '!' reads only if both strands lie together as one stroke, the stone sits directly below as the dot, and there is no added jump ring; it is laid flat, so it cannot swing.
Brackets: one hoop must be turned in its own plane; stripes may multiply or the C close. One redo budgeted.
The '&' is the weakest glyph: if the panel cannot read it, the card runs as 'TU [ring] MAIN.' with the meaning in the beat.
Pearl (25), Monochrome (24), Serpentine Silver (23) near the floor: never anchors.

camps.sources: surreal-1 (rank 7; it grows b04-3h, the best shipped ad, 8.19). Three are worn (two rings in a 9-10 cm hand crop, the Toggle at the nape with the camera directly behind the head); two are laid on black-and-white wedding silk with zari, the b04-3h grammar: the Circlet studs, because a stud's face cannot be seen from behind the head and the ear profile leaked the eye in both b02-3 tries, and the Prism, whose worn frames failed in b01 and b02 (red-team change). camps.brandDevice: Naira is the colour: every card grey except the piece and one word, so a viewer knows it is Naira before reading. F2 card in bone on charcoal. Primary-text sign-off 'Only Naira came in colour.'

Toggle + Halo Curve + Eternity ₹2,947 → ₹2,358: up to ₹472.

Worn scale (Toggle clasp 22 mm; rings within 1.2x).

camps.name: CHAAND TAARE (his list, the sky delivered)
camps.sources: surreal-2 PETITE, AGAINST THE SKY (rank 18; Rohan 8.5) for the picture device, merged with roas5-4 MAA. DIDI. AUR WOH. (rank 16) for the young man's three-recipient list. Changed: 'aur woh' (the other woman, from the film title) becomes 'AUR JUST A FRIEND.' (what he calls her at home); new card 1 'MAA SAID SHE WANTS NOTHING.' (every Indian mother's line); the piece is evenly front-lit and the brightest near object (backlight silhouettes); a low hazy sun and a full moon only; never a crescent with a star; no logos on the giant wheel.

forecast.roasBand: 2.5-4 on men 18-24, upside from women forwarding it (judgement)

camps.insight: A young man of 18-24 owes three gifts a season (his mother, his sister, the girl) with one budget, no confidence in his taste and no idea of anyone's size. Hindi film songs promised 'chaand taare tod laaun' (I'll pluck you the moon and stars). Here his fingertips hold the piece at true size against the sky so it lines up with the moon, a star or the sun: the promise kept, honestly, with the fingertips as the ruler. Three people, one order, nothing to size.
camps.pictureDevice: Honest forced perspective: his thumb and forefinger (clean short nails, entering from the right edge at the piece's height so the hand stays inside the picture band and nothing rises through the card zone; no face; any chain gathered round his finger, never hanging below the piece) hold one piece at true size close to a long lens, lined up with a giant distant thing it rhymes with (the full moon behind the pearl, the evening star beside the stone, wedding fireworks behind the two hearts, the setting sun inside the hoop, the lit giant wheel of a winter mela behind the halo). Blue-hour sky, navy to apricot; the jewellery evenly front-lit and the brightest near object.
camps.typeDevice: Velista H1 in bone high in the sky; Cormorant beat with the listing truth; card size in plain mm (the fingertips are the ruler, so no 'magnified' tag); the 'Naira Petite' wordmark high in the sky like a constellation.
camps.brandDevice: 'Petite' against the biggest things in the sky; the same hand, angle and sky on all five; card 5 names his whole list.
camps.palette: blue hour: navy to apricot; warm bokeh
camps.buyers: Men 18-24 (the account's best male segment, almost all gifts) in their own ad set; women 35-54 who forward the MAA card to their sons; women 25-34 for the romance.
camps.roas: Men 18-24 already buy gifts on the account; the three-recipient list makes BUY3 his basket and 'no size needed' removes his biggest fear. Pearl + Ribbon + Cushion (maa, didi, her) ₹2,897 → ₹2,318 after BUY3: ROAS 5 at up to ₹464 a purchase. Pearl + Serpentine Silver + Cushion ₹3,097 → ₹2,478: up to ₹496. Honest target: men's cost per purchase must fall by more than half, so expect 3-4x on men, with upside from shares.

risks: A bright sun or moon turns the piece into a silhouette: ask for the result ('the jewellery evenly lit from the front, the brightest near object; the sky deep blue').
The alignment may miss; verify.
Hands: five natural fingers, no rings or watch; the piece within 1.2x true size against the 15 mm fingertip.
Never a crescent beside a star (reads as a religious symbol). No logos on the wheel. Pearl: sky only, no sea or water.
Pearl (25), Serpentine Silver (23), Ribbon (21) near the floor: card 5 anchors on the Cushion.

camps.sources: surreal-5 NOT ACTUAL SIZE (rank 12; the biggest thumb-stop of the 24). Graft: roas5-3 UNDER THE LOUPE's honesty boast as the size-box voice. Kept: the simplest shapes (satin, enamel, a single stone); every card says what it really fits; judged on cost per purchase, never CTR; a test cell against the c01 control. Red-team change (20 Nov): the piece is no longer enlarged to architectural size, which broke RULINGS §3 (every picture generated directly at true size), learnings rule 3 (the piece stays at true size) and PLAYBOOK §1.1 (an oversized product misstates scale). The same picture is now made honestly: the real piece at true size inside a museum-grade 1:50 architectural model of the room, so it still stands half as tall as the doorway, and the headline reveals that the room is the small thing. The forecast is the planner's for the giant version; the panel re-rates the camp before batch 10.

forecast.roasBand: 2-4 (judgement; a stop-power test; re-rated after the red-team change)

camps.insight: Luxury jewellers show monumental installations because scale signals value, and the brand's own name says Petite. Turn the joke round: shoot the real piece in a perfect 1:50 model of a quiet Indian room, so at first glance it is a monument and on the second look the room is the small thing. The headline says so out loud: not a giant hoop, a tiny verandah. She gets the presence and the honesty in one look, and the piece is never misstated.
camps.pictureDevice: A real piece at true size inside a museum-grade 1:50 architectural model of an empty Indian interior (a red-oxide verandah, a Chettinad hall, an indigo courtyard, a terracotta stairwell, a terracotta-walled room), lit like architecture in natural light with honest macro depth of field, so the model reads as a room first and as a model on the second look. At 1:50 a doorway is about 4 cm tall, so a 20 mm hoop stands half as tall as the door. The piece is the brightest and sharpest object; no figurines, no people, no furniture, no religious objects, no brands.
camps.typeDevice: A Velista two-beat: the piece is not giant, the room is tiny ('NOT A GIANT HOOP. / A TINY VERANDAH.'); a 2 px hairline box in Jost caps set like an architecture caption, the piece's size on line 1 ('SHOWN MAGNIFIED · ABOUT 20 MM' at 19+ px/mm, else 'THE HOOPS · ABOUT 20 MM') and 'THE ROOM · A 1:50 MODEL' on line 2.
camps.brandDevice: The deadpan size box is the brand's voice (a wry friend who never lies about size). Primary text closes 'Naira Petite. The room was the trick.'
camps.palette: red oxide and lime · teak and charcoal · indigo lime · terracotta
camps.buyers: Women 35-54 who respond to design-led luxury cues; women 25-34 share it.
camps.roas: The magnified product-only hero given a world, with the size box answering 'how big is it really?' before she clicks. Brushed + Monochrome + Pearl ₹2,897 → ₹2,318 after BUY3: ROAS 5 at up to ₹464 a purchase. Serpentine gold + Bold Nocturne + Brushed ₹3,297 → ₹2,638: up to ₹528 (only after stock re-reads). Kill rule: judge on cost per purchase; clicks without carts end the cell.
camps.carousel: Verandah, hall, courtyard, stairwell, room; card 5 (TINY ROOM. ACTUAL OFFER.) links to a BUY3 collection.
risks: The size box is mandatory on Feed and Story; a frame without it fails.

The model must read as a room at first glance and as a model on the second look: fine lime plaster, red-oxide tiles about 6 mm, carved pillars, tilt-shift macro depth of field; never a toy or a dollhouse with furniture or figures (the tiny-figures camp was dropped as concept-as-hero).

The piece must stay the sharpest, brightest object: the model's detail stays softer than the piece's own construction; verify the piece against its references as usual (enamel stripes, pavé, satin grain, basket on bail).
She may fear the piece is big: the H1 and the box always say what it is and what it fits.

Four of the five pieces sit near the floor (Serpentine gold 20, Bold Nocturne 20, Pearl 25, Monochrome 24).

placements.P1: Product-only, headline + card. In the 9:16 frame (1080 x 1920) the piece is centred on x 540 with its full extent (piece, shadow, referent) inside y 470-1000, so the extent is at most about 540 px tall in 1080-wide units (the RULINGS gate is 550; a round piece seen face-on is therefore at most about half the Feed width, and every share in §4 is set to this cap); a chain or prop may leave the frame only through the left or right edge inside that band, never through the headline, wordmark or card zones; y 270-460 stays calm for the headline; y 1000-1920 is calm ground (Story card y 1000-1250, then Meta's UI zone). Feed = the 4:5 window at T ≈ 90 px (object-position P ≈ 15), which puts the extent at Feed y ≈ 380-910 (the RULINGS gate 380-930), the headline at Feed y 150-360 and the card block at Feed y 920-1250 (wordmark moves to top-centre y 84 when a headline is present). A 1:1 fallback crop (central square, Feed y 135-1215) keeps the piece and the headline; the carousel runs at 4:5. Prompt wording: 'the jewellery centred slightly above the middle of the frame, its height about H% of the frame height (0.7x the share wanted); the top fifth and the lower half are calm, empty ground'. The headline block (H1 with its beat) must fit Feed y 150-360 (about 210 px): the H1 sizes in §4 are maxima, and a two-line H1 drops to 84 px.

As P1, but the piece sits right of centre (or at the end of the line) with calm ground to its left or between its parts for the Velista words, which stay 30+ px clear of metal. Extent still inside 9:16 y 470-1000 (at most about 540 px tall); a glyph whose chain must leave the frame uses P1 instead (words above, chain out through a side edge).

A calm, darker area (velvet, blouse, hair, sky) carries the headline in Story y 290-480 and the card in Story y 1000-1250, with a scrim in the ground colour only if busy. Feed window T ≈ 150 (P ≈ 26). The Story is the whole 9:16 frame, so the face gate is checked on all 1920 px, not the Feed window: no eye, brow or nose anywhere in it; where lips appear (c07-3 only) the top edge cuts through the lower lip. Ears and nape from directly behind or back three-quarter, the face physically hidden behind the head (b02); a stud is never worn from behind, because the lobe hides its face. A hand that holds a piece enters from a side edge inside the band.

process.name: Pre-flight (read-only, before every batch)
process.detail: Read the Higgsfield balance (another session spends on this account). Read Shopify live for the batch's five products: price, stock of every variant shown (20+), tags that allow claims; read the offer codes (NAIRA10, BUY2, BUY3, BUY4: values and minimums). Apply the stock gates and swaps written on each ad: swaps resolve in batch order, a swap that would take any product past 5 uses falls to the ad's next option, and the last option is always to drop the card (the camp then runs 4 cards plus its offer card, and the unused credits go to the reserve). Re-read RULINGS.md and learnings rules 1-17. Apply the previous batch's loop note to this batch's briefs and log the diff (at least one change, or 'none, because ...'). If BUY4 is not cleared by the owner, every BUY4 box falls back to BUY3.

process.name: Balance read and go/no-go
process.detail: Go only if balance ≥ the batch's planned credits + 6.25 (one spare redo or clip). If short: cut that batch's clips first, then its planned redos, then defer the batch and cut the lowest-ranked remaining camp (c10 first, then c09).

process.name: Five stills
process.detail: nano_banana_pro, 9:16, 2K, one picture per ad, all generated directly (no plates, no edit passes, nothing reused). Slot 1 = the listing reference named on the ad (the authority), slot 2 = a detail of the same piece only. Every prompt carries: the product lock (countable construction + one 'must stay X, never Y' clause), scale built in mm plus the referent, light described by its result, the placement standard (P1-P5), the ground/palette, a neutrality clause on coloured grounds ('clear stones stay colourless, white enamel stays white, warm-white pearl stays neutral, no colour cast on the metal'), 'no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos', and for worn frames 'no eyes, no eyebrows, no nose'. One batch call; 10 credits. Log the model that actually served each job (in b01-b03 every job asked for nano_banana_pro was served as nano_banana_2).

process.name: Verify each still against its reference
process.detail: At 1x and 2x zoom with crops beside the reference at the same crop: construction (clasp, latch, bail, halo rows, S-wave, circlet asymmetry), counts (stripes, stones, hearts, bridges, colours), colour (casts on pearl, enamel, clear stones, gold warm-neutral), scale (pixel ruler: px/mm against the referent; worn within 1.2x; product-only px/mm decides 'Shown magnified' at 19+), connectors (no added jump ring, no invented loop), faces, text/logos, device rendered yes/no (rule 14), and the placement gate (some window T puts the extent inside Feed y 380-930). Log everything in batches/cNN/verify.md.

process.name: One redo for a failed still
process.detail: A failed still is regenerated once, with the named fault fixed in the prompt ('the bar is 0.6-0.7x the ring; last time it was as long as the ring'). A redo that fails again ends that slot: the camp runs the remaining cards and the offer moves to the last valid card (RULINGS: once at most). Redos come from the batch's allocation, then from the reserve.

process.name: Graphic design: three variations per ad
process.detail: Kit only (Velista caps, Cormorant Garamond italic, Jost; the F2 card; tokens; render.cjs gates). For each ad: V1 = the planned headline, beat and layout; V2 = the first alternate headline (or the second beat swapped); V3 = a layout variant (hook moved into the card line as a card-only frame, or the headline larger/smaller and repositioned, or the price/offer emphasis changed). Feed 1080x1350 and Story 1080x1920 for each; render.cjs must report no font fallback, no text outside the safe area, nothing under 26 px (22 px footnotes), at most 4 text elements.

process.name: Blind rating of the three
process.detail: Coded tiles, random order, no key. The three experts of §7 (performance buyer, craft creative director, production and truth verifier), each fresh to the batch, score PLAYBOOK §7 (stop .15, one message .10, truth .15, layout .10, brand .05, copy .10, archetype .05, desire .15, purchase cues .15) plus a 200 px read on a coded sheet that carries one winner anchor and one loser anchor (rotated, rule 12). Three customer personas chosen for the camp's buyer (always Meera 38; plus two of Sunita 48, Ananya 29, Rohan 22; Rohan always for c09, the reversed c01 set and the men's single ads) score stop, want, trust and would-buy (1-10, and yes/no) and name the 3 pieces they would put in the basket. Each critic runs twice; the runs are averaged (rule 15).

process.name: Pick the best
process.detail: Gate: compliance passes, truth ≥ 8, no §7 dimension under 6, the performance buyer and the craft director both beat the loser anchor at 200 px (the RULINGS 'both critics' rule). Among those passing: 0.5 x expert §7 weighted mean + 0.3 x customer would-buy mean + 0.2 x 200 px read. Ties go to the variant whose customers named a 3-piece basket more often. The two runner-up variants are kept as `<id>h` headline variants only when they change words alone (never a new ad).

process.name: Animate the chosen animated ads
process.detail: Kling 3.0 image-to-video, 5 s, silent, 9:16, from the verified raw still (never from the designed ad). Prompt: camera behaviour, 'the jewellery is rigid and keeps its exact shape, stones and colours', and the one thing that moves. Verify every frame (shape, stone count and order, colour bleed, hands); cut at the last clean frame. Type and the F2 card are overlaid static in the layout; the card holds the last 1.5 s. A morphing clip gets one camera-only retry (push-in) from the reserve, else the ad ships as the still.

process.name: Carousel assembly
process.detail: One 5-card carousel per camp at 4:5 (1080x1350; the 1:1 crop is the fallback, safe because every piece sits inside the central square). Card 1 = the strongest thumb-stop (never a title card); cards 2-4 vary the body part; card 5 = the BUY3 (or BUY4) card. One series look per camp (ground, card position, type sizes, counters). Each card links to its own product page with UTMs; card 5 links to a collection. Primary text 120-180 characters: the hook, the offer's verified value before character 125, 'Every piece here is in stock.', COD only if the pre-flight read confirms it. The same rule holds for every single ad, not only card 5: each ad's primary text is its hook plus the camp's BUY3 line (c01: 'Two to gift, one to keep: 20% off any three with BUY3.'), so every placement asks for three. Card 5's collection is read live at pre-flight and must hold only in-stock eligible pieces; if none exists, card 5 links to its own product page and the BUY3 line carries the offer.

process.name: Final checks
process.detail: Banned-word lint on copy, prompts and file names (diamond, real/solid gold, gold or silver alone as the metal, freshwater, emerald/ruby as nouns); claims only where allowed (never Pearl or Monochrome; no water for Toggle); live prices and stock; offer values; no compare-at, no struck price, no price sum, no free shipping; 'Silver' in the Serpentine Silver name; size line rule (19 px/mm); every Story prints an offer (rule 13); the picture proves the headline (rule 17); copy.json per ad (primary text, headline, description, CTA, URL with UTMs). Nothing is uploaded to Meta.

process.name: Loop note
process.detail: The expert panel and the customer panel rate the five finished ads; the lead writes the loop note (below) and edits the next batch's briefs before its pre-flight. Append the batch to build/learnings and the ledger.

loop.rule: Redo the next 5 better: no batch starts until the previous batch's loop note has changed its briefs (prompt clauses, copy, layout, product or order), and the change is logged as a diff. 'No change' is allowed only with a reason.
expertPanel: Performance buyer (ROAS, cost per purchase, purchase cues, basket logic)
Craft creative director (stop power, layout, one message, brand series, award-level wit)
Production and truth verifier (fidelity, scale, casts, compliance)
customerPanel: Meera, 38, Pune: three December weddings; the core buyer (women 35-44)
Sunita, 48, Lucknow: mother of a groom this season; women 45-54
Ananya, 29, Bengaluru: design-literate, office Secret Santa; women 25-34
Rohan, 22, Delhi: student, buys gifts for maa, didi and his girlfriend; men 18-24
loop.ratings: Each panellist rates every finished ad 1-10 (experts: §7 weighted + 200 px read; customers: stop, want, trust, would-buy yes/no and the 3 pieces they would buy) and gives one line. The batch's expert mean, customer mean and basket rate (share of customer answers naming 3+ pieces) are recorded.
noteFields: scores (expert mean, customer mean, per ad, basket rate)
fix target: the lowest §7 dimension across the batch, with the change that fixes it in the next batch
one new move tried in the next batch
keep: what worked and is carried forward (named device, prompt clause, layout)
drop: what failed and is banned for the rest of the run
brief diff: the exact edits to the next batch's five briefs
verification lessons: every redo's cause and the prompt clause that fixed it
credits spent and balance; stock re-read
thresholds: Batch pass: expert mean ≥ 7.8 AND customer mean ≥ 7.8 AND at least 4 of 5 ads ship.
Basket check: if fewer than half of the customer answers name 3 pieces, the next batch strengthens card 5 and the primary text (bigger offer box, a named trio, 'two to gift, one to keep' logic).
If a batch's customer mean is more than 0.5 below its expert mean, the next batch adds desire (warmer light, an occasion in the picture, a worn or hand cue) without losing the 200 px read.
If a batch's expert 200 px read loses to the loser anchor on 2+ ads, the next batch enlarges the piece (to the upper end of its share band) and calms the ground.
A device that beats the winner anchor with both experts in two batches becomes a rule in learnings (house rule).
A camp whose mean is under 7.0 is not reused; the next camp that shares its risk is re-briefed, or swapped for the bench.
loop.replanPoints: After batch 3 and batch 6 the lead re-ranks the remaining camps with everything learned (scores, redo causes, customer baskets, credits) and may swap one camp for a bench camp or reorder.
bench: typewit-4 CAPTIONED ('[collective gasp]', '[Mummy, off screen: teeno le lo.]'): best as a Reels camp if the c05 clips work
typewit-2 THE ITINERARY (pieces as the zeros of '8:00 PM'): only if c03 sells
typewit-5 ATTEMPT ANY THREE: retargeting only
roas5-3 UNDER THE LOUPE: the trust layer behind a desire camp

reserveRules: Unused redo or clip credits roll forward to the next batch.

The reserve (20.46) pays for: redos beyond a batch's allocation (each still is still regenerated once at most), one camera-only retry of a morphing clip, and at most one clip the loop promotes (a 9th clip only if the reserve stays ≥ 6 after it).
Read the balance before every batch; if the live balance is below the remaining plan, cut in this order: c10's clip, c09's clip, unspent redo allocations, then the whole of c10, then c09.
Stop when the balance is under 2 (the cost of one picture).

panelNote: Panel = the ranking's expert mean and customer-panel mean for the source camp (merged sources shown in brackets). Forecast = the lead planner's rating of the sharpened camp as an ads expert and as the customer (judgement, not data).
